messages.subject: Re: surface models from nat.flybrains
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jan,

Thanks for asking about appropriate citation. The answer depends on what
you are using.

If you are using the FCWB template then you should cite Chiang et al
2011 for the raw image data and Costa et al 2016 for the construction of
the template and surface models.

If you are using any of the cross registration tools (to move data
between template brains) then you should for the time being cite Manton
et al 2014 biorXiv – we hope to have a formal publication on this
sooner rather than later.

Of course you should point to the repository when you write up your
methods, but regrettably the only citations that help to support the
continued development of these kind of tools are those to journal
articles contained within the main body (not SI) of a paper.

All the best,

Greg.

messages.subject: Re: Drosophila Image Registration Question
messages.body_plain:
Dear Tyler,

You may be able to carry out some kind of registration but it probably
won't be with CMTK. Depending on what other features are visible in your
images, you may be able to choose some landmarks that you could use to
drive e.g. a thin plate spline or moving least squares registrations.

That said, the antennal lobe is a particularly variable part of the
brain and without having a neuropil stain I would be wary of drawing
strong conclusions about which glomeruli are innervated.

Best wishes,

Greg Jefferis.

PS I have taken the liberty of ccing this message to the nat-user google
group since the answer may be of interest to others.

messages.body_plain:
Greg,

I see.  Alternatively, would it be possible for me to do a "reverse" GAL4 NBLAST? Some way of inputing the Janelia GAL4 driver I am using, and then receive the traces for the neurons included in that driver.

Essentially, the same operation you would perform to identify a driver from FlyLight that may contain your neuron-of-interest (based on the FlyCircuit identifier of your neuron), but in reverse.

Best Regards,

Tyler

messages.subject: Re: flycircuit neurons in NAT
messages.body_plain:
Dear Jamie

Nice to hear from you! Hope you are settling in well at Yale.

What you see is actually the result of the relatively simple
representation of neurons in the `dotprops` format that we use for
NBLAST. Neurons are represented as a series of short unconnected
segments order 1 micron apart. These look pretty jagged when you zoom
in.

You can read more about this format at
http://jefferis.github.io/nat/reference/dotprops.html and in the NBLAST
paper
(https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0896627316302653?via%3Dihub#sec2).

Best wishes,

Greg.

PS I have taken the liberty of ccing this message to the nat-user google
group since the answer may be of interest to others.

--
